tasks.title: Docker & Env De-ambiguation - Configure docker-compose.yml with single PROJECTS_HOST_DIR mount, update .env settings, set database projects.path to container paths, rebuild and test containers
tasks.description: Simplify Docker configuration by consolidating project mounts into a single PROJECTS_HOST_DIR variable, update environment settings, and configure database to use container paths for improved consistency and maintainability.
tasks.details:
1. Update docker-compose.yml to use single PROJECTS_HOST_DIR environment variable:
   - Replace multiple project-specific volume mounts with ${PROJECTS_HOST_DIR}:/projects
   - Ensure all containers use consistent /projects mount point
   - Remove redundant volume definitions

2. Update .env file settings:
   - Define PROJECTS_HOST_DIR=E:\projects (Windows host path)
   - Remove duplicate or conflicting project path variables
   - Document the new simplified mounting structure

3. Configure database projects.path field:
   - Update all project records to use container paths (/projects/project-name)
   - Migrate existing host paths to container equivalents
   - Add validation to ensure paths start with /projects/

4. Update application code:
   - Modify path resolution logic to work with container paths
   - Update any hardcoded path references
   - Ensure cross-platform compatibility

5. Rebuild containers with no cache:
   - Run docker-compose down --volumes
   - Execute docker-compose build --no-cache
   - Start containers with docker-compose up -d

6. Verify mount points and path resolution:
   - Test that /projects directory is accessible in containers
   - Confirm project files are visible at expected paths
   - Validate database path entries work correctly
tasks.testStrategy:
1. Verify docker-compose.yml syntax and PROJECTS_HOST_DIR variable usage
2. Confirm .env file contains correct PROJECTS_HOST_DIR path
3. Test container rebuild process completes without errors
4. Validate /projects mount point exists in all containers
5. Check that project directories are accessible at /projects/project-name paths
6. Test database project records use container paths (/projects/...)
7. Verify application can read/write project files using new paths
8. Test project creation and access through web interface
9. Confirm no broken path references remain in logs
10. Validate cross-container file access works correctly
11. Test backup and restore functionality with new path structure
